Article Title: ChatGPT gave Google 'Code Red’, prompting co-founder Sergey Brin's return; Now OpenAI’s Greg Brockman is facing 'Red Flag'
Article Text:
Greg Brockman goes into ‘founder mode’

OpenAI witnessing a wave of high-profile departures

In December 2022, the meteoric rise of ChatGPT reportedly triggered a “Code Red” inside Google . The situation led co-founder Sergey Brin back into hands-on technical development. Fast forward to August 2026, the tables have turned, presenting OpenAI leadership led by CEO Sam Altman and president Greg Brockman (both cofounders) with what industry analysts are calling a major “red flag” of their own.A wave of high-profile executive departures is shaking the AI company’s front office at a critical juncture, as the artificial intelligence (AI) giant prepares for an anticipated initial public offering ( IPO ) while seeking to validate an $852 billion valuation.Meanwhile, citing sources familiar to the matter, a report by Axios claims that Brockman is getting more involved in the company’s day-to-day operations to contain disruptions. Brockman is said to be meeting with more customers and teams across the company than ever before. Brockman is said to be publicly framing the departures as a change in corporate focus.The latest blow came with the resignation of chief revenue officer Denise Dresser after less than a year at the company. Dresser, a seasoned software executive who previously spent over a decade at Salesforce and Slack, was recruited in December to spearhead OpenAI's enterprise commercial strategy against formidable rivals like Anthropic.Her departure landed just two days after longtime COO and senior executive, Brad Lightcap, announced his own exit after eight years, leaving key corporate divisions in transition. Her profile expanded significantly four months later when she took over operational duties previously handled by Lightcap. However, Dresser's abrupt departure compounds a broader pattern of senior leadership churn.For example, Fidji Simo, the former Instacart CEO stepped away from her high-ranking OpenAI executive role in July to focus on managing a chronic illness. Four other senior leaders, including former VP of Science Kevin Weil and CMO Kate Rouch, left the company in April. The exits arrive only months after OpenAI submitted a confidential IPO draft registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission, raising concerns among private market watchers.“The executives leaving OpenAI ahead of their IPO is a huge red flag,” noted Kevin McCormick, founder of AI startup SignAudit.AI, pointing out that walking away before a liquidity event suggests underlying tensions.“If the executives leaving aren’t being ‘made whole’ by the next company, it’s bad news for OpenAI,” McCormick wrote, as per a report by CNBC.Meanwhile, Dali Rajic – former COO of cybersecurity firm Wiz – joined as chief revenue officer. OpenAI also hired top AI researcher Noam Shazeer from Google in June 2026. He is a co-inventor of the foundational transformer architecture and former co-lead of Google’s Gemini models, and joined OpenAI to head Architecture Research.
Article Summary: A wave of high-profile executive departures is shaking the AI company’s front office at a critical juncture. The exits arrive only months after OpenAI submitted a confidential IPO draft registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The latest blow came with the resignation of chief revenue officer Denise Dresser.

Article Title: Accenture CEO Julie Sweet makes a 'vacation request' to employees for this August
Article Text:
Julie Sweet asks employees to help deliver a strong fourth quarter

Why Accenture changed its vacation policy

AI remains a key concern for Accenture investors

Accenture CEO Julie Sweet is asking employees to think twice before taking time off this August as the company pushes for a strong finish to its financial year. In a rare one-time policy change, Accenture will allow staff to carry forward any unused vacation days into the next fiscal year instead of requiring them to use the leave before August ends. The move comes alongside Julie Sweet's call for employees to focus on winning new business and generating more revenue in the final weeks of the quarter after the consulting giant reported weaker-than-expected quarterly results. Accenture’s new policy will give its workers more flexibility while helping keep more employees available during the company's year-end sales push.In a memo seen by Bloomberg, Accenture CEO Julie Sweet urged employees to contribute to improving fourth-quarter results by finding new ways to serve clients and generate revenue. "Our shareholders are counting on us to deliver a strong quarter in Q4 — everyone can contribute," Sweet wrote.“This means we all need to find more ways to serve clients that create more revenue in the quarter and to originate more sales (small, large, mega) to finish strong,” she added.According to Bloomberg, the company has also allowed employees to carry over unused vacation days into the next financial year, which begins on September 1.Normally, staff must use their vacation before the fiscal year ends.People familiar with the matter told the publication that the temporary policy change is part of the company's effort to keep more employees working during August rather than taking leave before their vacation days expire. Another person familiar with the matter said the one-time change is also meant to give employees greater flexibility.The move comes after weaker-than-expected results. Accenture reported a 2% decline in new bookings for the quarter ended May 31 and projected fourth-quarter revenue of $17.75 billion to $18.4 billion, below analysts' average estimate of $18.47 billion. Following the earnings announcement in June, Accenture shares fell about 20% in one day, one of the company's biggest single-day declines on record.The earnings report also intensified concerns that artificial intelligence could disrupt the consulting industry in the near term, even though Julie Sweet has described AI as a "tailwind" for Accenture's business.Bloomberg Intelligence said in a recent research note: “AI remains the dominant concern for services and consulting. Though management positions Accenture as a long-term AI beneficiary, tangible evidence that AI is accelerating demand is limited.”
Article Summary: Accenture will allow staff to carry forward any unused vacation days into the next fiscal year instead of requiring them to use the leave before August ends. The move comes alongside Julie Sweet's call for employees to focus on winning new business and generating more revenue in the final weeks of the quarter.

Article Title: ‘10 online shopping platforms that faced most consumer complaints, non-delivery of goods top grievance; Rs 91 crore refunds in one year’
Article Text:
​10 online shopping platforms that faced most consumer complaints

Top 10 E-Commerce Platforms by Grievance Volume

Regulatory crackdown and refunds

How NCH complaint system works

Online shopping giants Flipkart, Amazon and Meesho emerged as the top three platforms facing the highest volume of consumer grievances on the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) in 2025, the government informed the Lok Sabha recently. In a written reply to the Parliament, Union Minister of State for Consumer Affairs BL Verma disclosed that Flipkart topped the list with over 1.33 lakh complaints, followed by Amazon with 91,248 and Meesho with 29,284. Quick-commerce and niche retail platforms also featured prominently among the top ten offenders.Operated by the Department of Consumer Affairs, the NCH acts as a single-window pre-litigation website. It currently supports 17 Indian languages and connects consumers with 1,853 partner companies registered under its voluntary "Convergence" initiative. This means that consumers can lodge complaints in 17 languages, including Hindi, English, Kashmiri, Punjabi, Nepali, Gujarati, Marathi, Kannada, Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, Maithili, Santhali, Bengali, Odia, Assamese and Manipuri, through the toll-free number 1915.* Flipkart: 1,33,000* Amazon: 91,248* Meesho: 29,284* Myntra: 25,384* Netmeds: 19,895* Zepto: 5,774* Blinkit: 5,102* Naaptol: 4,079* VLE Bazaar: 3,907* Nykaa: 3,405To curb unfair trade practices under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) imposed fines on 47 platforms, slapping collective fines totaling approximately Rs 1.12 crore (Rs 1,12,01,500). The minister highlighted significant enforcement outcomes through pre-litigation resolution.The minister said that the NCH facilitated refunds of over Rs 91 crore to consumers between April 25, 2025, and June 30, 2026, of which more than Rs 63 crore pertained to grievances in the e-commerce sector. This was achieved by resolving over 1,47,000 consumer grievances related to refund claims at the pre-litigation stage, he said. A total of 5.11 lakh complaints related to quick commerce were received on the NCH in 2025, all of which were disposed of, the minister added.Non-delivery of products was the single largest category of complaints in 2025, accounting for 79,818 cases. Other frequent complaints included delivery of the wrong product, denial of replacement or refund as per policy, delivery of defective or damaged goods, non-refund of paid amounts, deficiency in services, sale of spurious or counterfeit products, and unauthorised debit of amounts without consumer consent.Consumers can escalate unresolved e-commerce disputes through:* Toll-Free Helpline: 1915* WhatsApp / SMS: 8800001915* Email: nch-ca@gov.in* Complaint websites: consumerhelpline.gov.in, the NCH app, and the UMANG application
Article Summary: Flipkart topped the list with over 1.33 lakh complaints, followed by Amazon with 91,248 and Meesho with 29,284. Quick-commerce and niche retail platforms also featured prominently among the top ten offenders. Non-delivery of products was the single largest category of complaints, accounting for 79,818 cases.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos: “I think frugality drives innovation, just like other constraints do. One of…”
Article Text:
Image: AP News

Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos

“I think frugality drives innovation, just like other constraints do. One of the only ways to get out of a tight box is to invent your way out.”

What does this quote mean?

Limitations can force us to think differently

Necessity has a long history of creating innovation

Frugality can make innovation more efficient

Constraints can turn problems into creative challenges

Creativity often grows outside the comfort zone

Why this quote still matters today

Innovation is often associated with having more, more money, more resources, more advanced technology and more time. But some of the most creative solutions emerge when those advantages are limited. Jeff Bezos captured this idea when he said, “I think frugality drives innovation, just like other constraints do. One of the only ways to get out of a tight box is to invent your way out.” His words suggest that limitations do not always prevent progress. Sometimes, they force people to think differently, question familiar methods and find solutions that would never have emerged in more comfortable circumstances.Jeff Bezos (1964-present) is an American entrepreneur and founder of Amazon. He built the company from an online bookseller into one of the world's largest technology and e-commerce businesses and has also pursued ventures in space exploration through Blue Origin.This statement implies that scarcity of resources can be an impetus for innovation. When there are no simple solutions, people are obliged to rethink how to do things.Tight budget, shortage of materials, or technical difficulties can become the grounds for experimenting rather than excuses for inaction. The main message that Bezos tries to convey here is that constraints can make people innovative.In the case of abundance of resources, it is easy to find a solution by adding more resources, people, tools or funds. Constraints take away that luxury. All of a sudden, efficiency becomes the priority, and common assumptions should be questioned. A constrained team might discover a simpler way of doing things just because they do not have enough means to operate according to the traditional way.Useful innovations have often been developed due to people’s needs for solving certain problems using what was already available at hand. In cases ranging from simple farming implements to sophisticated medical gadgets that operate in conditions of limited resources, necessity has proved time and again to breed creativity. In the absence of an apparent solution, people start to search for other ways of solving their problems.Innovation does not necessarily mean that you should develop something that is larger or more complicated than your current product. Some of the most outstanding solutions come when people try to do the same thing using less material resources or reducing superfluous steps in a process. This way, frugality may become another incentive for inventors to find what really matters.It may seem as if a hard constraint makes the issue a roadblock. However, perceiving a limitation as a challenge will make a difference in the mindset when it comes to dealing with an issue. The question from “Why can't we do this?” will turn into “How could we do this differently?” This approach can foster experimenting and coming up with unique ideas.Comfort can help one to carry on with the things as usual. Constraints break up the sense of comfort. They make one think and come up with new options. Regardless of whether one is starting a business, developing a product or even solving a simple problem, constraints can provide a different perspective of creativity than abundance can.Whether it be startups trying to innovate on meager resources or scientists innovating the technology to suit a harsh environment, innovations often emerge when there is a sense of urgency involved. The words of Jeff Bezos provide an excellent point that lack of resources should not necessarily translate into lack of opportunities. In some cases, the very fact that there is no easy way out leads to innovation of a solution. The lesson from the statement is quite straightforward: Innovation occurs when nothing else works.
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos is an American entrepreneur and founder of Amazon. He said, “I think frugality drives innovation, just like other constraints do. One of the only ways to get out of a tight box is to invent your way out.” His words suggest that limitations do not always prevent progress.

Article Title: How Google's parent Alphabet turned into the biggest profitable shareholder after SpaceX's IPO
Article Text:
A historic return on venture capital

Concentration among top institutional backers

Fidelity investments is ranked as the second-largest institutional shareholder with 302.6 million shares.

Gigafund management reported holding 171.8 million shares.

Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) disclosed a 154.1 million-share position valued at $26.3 billion at the end of the second quarter.

Baillie Gifford & BlackRock reported stakes of 51.4 million and 51.0 million shares, respectively.

Other major holders include Brookfield Corp. with 19.2 million shares, Hancock Prospecting with 8 million shares valued at $1.4 billion, Balyasny Asset Management with 3.4 million shares, and Tiger Global Management holding 375,000 shares.

Alphabet’s decade-old gamble on Elon Musk’s space company has delivered a lucrative return, turning Google’s parent company into the largest institutional shareholder following SpaceX’s blockbuster initial public offering (IPO). Citing quarterly regulatory disclosures, news agency Reuters reports that Alphabet held a position valued at approximately $94.2 billion at the end of June. The valuation stems from an original $900 million investment made in SpaceX back in 2015 – representing a huge gain of more than 100 times its starting capital.SpaceX completed an $86 billion public listing in June, providing the first clear public window into the enormous stakes accumulated by early institutional backers while the rocket and satellite company operated as a private startup.According to Alphabet’s second-quarter 13F regulatory filing, the tech giant held 551.2 million SpaceX shares as of June 30, when the aerospace manufacturer was trading at $170.86 per share. Even with normal post-IPO stock fluctuations adjusting the market value of the position to around $77.9 billion by mid-August, Alphabet’s holding still stands at roughly 86.5 times the size of its initial 2015 check.Market analysts noted that while tracking precise institutional entry prices across multiple funding rounds is challenging, Alphabet’s publicly documented $900 million transaction in 2015 offers a clear baseline illustrating how private-market aerospace valuation translated into massive public market gains, the report added.The latest round of regulatory filings also outlines the broader distribution of SpaceX shares across global asset managers and sovereign wealth funds.
Article Summary: Alphabet is the largest institutional shareholder of SpaceX, according to regulatory filings. Fidelity investments is ranked as the second-largest institutional shareholder with 302.6 million shares. Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) disclosed a 154.1 million-share position valued at $26.3 billion at the end of June.

Nvidia discloses $21 billion stake in SpaceX

Article Title: Quote of the day by Jensen Huang, ‘The more you buy, the more you save’
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Jensen Huang

What Jensen Huang's quote means

Why the line resonates (and gets mocked)

Applying the idea beyond semiconductors

A simple takeaway

Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has spent more than three decades steering it from a scrappy graphics chip maker into the company at the center of the global AI boom, with Nvidia's GPUs now powering everything from video games to the largest AI models in the world. Along the way, Huang has developed a reputation not just for technical vision but for blunt, often counterintuitive one-liners delivered on stage at Nvidia's keynotes. Few have generated as much discussion, and as much good-natured mockery, as this one."The more you buy, the more you save."On its face, the quote sounds like it inverts basic financial logic — spending more money is not usually how anyone ends up saving money. Huang himself has acknowledged the tension directly, once following the line up by calling it "CEO math," adding that it's "not accurate, but it is correct." That qualifier is doing a lot of work. He isn't claiming the arithmetic checks out in a literal sense. He's arguing that from a strategic, systems-level view, larger upfront investment in the right infrastructure can produce disproportionate long-term returns, even if the sticker price climbs.The context matters here. Huang has used the line specifically to describe investment in Nvidia's GPU and networking infrastructure for AI data centers. His argument is that building at scale, investing heavily in accelerated computing rather than trying to get by with smaller, incremental upgrades, ultimately reduces the total cost and energy required to do the same amount of computing work. In other words, the "saving" isn't in the sense of holding onto more cash today. It's in the efficiency gained per unit of computation once the larger system is up and running.Part of what makes the quote memorable is exactly the tension it plays with. It sounds like a walking cliché of corporate spin, the kind of thing said to justify a big expense after the fact. That's precisely why it's been widely shared, sometimes sincerely as an illustration of infrastructure economics, and sometimes as a punchline, including consumer tech outlets jokingly applying the phrase to PC-building shopping sprees that were anything but frugal.But there's a real principle underneath the joke. In large-scale computing, cost efficiency often doesn't scale linearly. A company that invests in a fully built-out, high-performance system can end up paying less per unit of useful output than one that buys smaller, cheaper components piecemeal and stitches them together inefficiently. Huang's framing asks decision-makers to evaluate cost per outcome rather than sticker price in isolation, a shift in thinking that applies well beyond chips and data centers.The logic behind "CEO math" shows up in other investment decisions too, when approached carefully. Buying a higher-quality tool or system upfront, one built to handle a job well rather than just adequately, can reduce the long-run cost of inefficiency, breakdowns, or having to redo work later. The same reasoning applies to hiring, education, or infrastructure of almost any kind: the cheapest option today isn't automatically the cheapest option over time.The caveat, and it's an important one, is that this logic only holds when the larger investment is actually well-targeted. Spending more without a clear efficiency payoff isn't strategic, it's just spending more. Huang's own framing depends entirely on the assumption that the additional expense buys genuine capability and efficiency gains, not simply a bigger price tag.The quote works best as a prompt to look past the initial cost of a decision and ask what it actually buys in terms of long-term value. The next time a larger upfront investment feels wasteful on the surface, the more useful question isn't "is this expensive?" but "does this genuinely reduce cost or increase output per dollar over time?" Huang's line is deliberately provocative precisely because it forces that question into the open, even while admitting, with a wink, that the math doesn't quite add up the way it sounds.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has spent more than three decades steering it from a scrappy graphics chip maker into the center of the global AI boom. Huang has developed a reputation not just for technical vision but for blunt, often counterintuitive one-liners delivered on stage at Nvidia's keynotes.

Article Title: Can I use soapy water to clean TV screen? Here’s what you should know
Article Text:
Tips to to clean TV screen safely (AI-generated image)

How to clean TV screen safely with soap

Dip a clean microfiber cloth into the solution

Wring it out thoroughly so it is only slightly damp.

Wipe the screen gently using light, circular motions without pressing hard.

Once clean, use a dry microfiber cloth to remove any remaining moisture.

Things that you should never use to clean your TV screen

Never use glass cleaner on a TV screen

Avoid paper towels

Don't use household cleaning sprays

Skip rubbing alcohol and harsh chemicals

Never spray water directly on the screen

Don't use rough cloths or old rags

Avoid excessive pressure while cleaning

Avoid baby wipes or wet wipes

Don't use abrasive sponges or scrubbers

Cleaning a TV screen looks like a simple job, but the wrong product or tool can scratch the display, strip its protective coating, or cause permanent damage. Modern LED, OLED, QLED and Mini-LED televisions come with delicate anti-glare and anti-reflective coatings that need careful handling. One question often asked is whether one can use soapy water to clean a TV screen? The short answer is: not directly. While a small amount of diluted soapy water may be recommended for stubborn stains, using too much soap, spraying liquid directly on the display, can damage the screen's protective coating or allow moisture to seep inside the TV.If you need to remove stubborn fingerprints or greasy marks, use only a very small amount of mild dish soap mixed with distilled water.Note: Avoid using strong detergents or excess soap, as they can damage the screen's protective coating.Experts say only approved cleaning methods should be used, and have flagged several household items that people commonly reach for by mistake. Here's a look at what to avoid when cleaning your TV screen, and why.Most glass cleaners contain ammonia, alcohol or other harsh chemicals that can damage the protective coating on modern displays.These products may work fine on windows or mirrors, but on a TV screen they can leave streaks and permanently alter its finish.Paper towels may feel soft, but they contain wood fibres that can scratch the screen over time. Addiitnally, they can also leave lint behind, making the display look dirtier after cleaning.Multi-purpose cleaners, kitchen cleaners and disinfectant sprays are not designed for electronics. Spraying them directly on the TV can damage its screen and may allow liquid to seep into the edges of the screen.Strong cleaning agents such as rubbing alcohol, acetone, bleach or ammonia-based products can strip away the anti-reflective coating found on many modern televisions. Once damaged, the coating cannot be restored.Water sprayed onto a display can run down and seep into the TV through its edges or vents, raising the risk of internal damage. If moisture is needed, a lightly dampened microfiber cloth is the safer route.Old T-shirts, towels, tissues and rough fabric can carry dirt or coarse fibres that scratch the display. A clean microfiber cloth remains the safest choice for wiping away dust and fingerprints.Pressing hard on the screen can damage the display panel, especially on OLED and LED TVs. Use light, gentle strokes instead of scrubbing stubborn marks.Wet wipes or for that matter baby wipes contain cleaning chemicals, fragrances or moisturisers that are not safe for TV screens. Using wet wipes on screen can leave residue and may damage the coating over time.Kitchen sponges, scouring pads or abrasive cleaning tools can permanently scratch the TV screen, even with gentle use. These products should never be used on electronic displays.
Article Summary: Cleaning a TV screen looks like a simple job, but the wrong product or tool can scratch the display, strip its protective coating, or cause permanent damage. Experts say only approved cleaning methods should be used, and have flagged several household items that people commonly reach for by mistake.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg and Merab Dvalishvili go 'fighting' in the middle of the sea, Meta CEO shares one-minute-plus video says: Merab made me ...
Article Text:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg: ‘Merab made me take my shirt off’

Mark Zuckerberg’s well-known MMA habit

The yacht controversy

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has taken his mixed martial arts training to new heights or rather new waters by sparring with former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili on a giant barge in the middle of Lake Tahoe. In a one-minute-plus video shared on Instagram, the pair traded blows in front of drones, videographers, and friends, with Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan casually paddling past on a canoe.Zuckerberg also joked in the one-minute clip that Dvalishvili insisted that he remove his shirt ‘because it looks more fighter.’ While the UFC star appeared to be going easy on the billionaire, Zuckerberg showcased striking and wrestling skills, even throwing Dvalishvili into the water. The sparring session marks the second time the duo have trained together, following a December 2025 meet-up.The footage captured multiple angles of the sparring rounds, with an array of cameras clearly set up in advance to document the encounter. At one point, Zuckerberg's wife Priscilla Chan is seen paddling past the barge on a canoe. Sharing the clip, Zuckerberg explained that Dvalishvili had told him to take his shirt off because it looks more fighter.Dvalishvili, who won the UFC bantamweight title in 2024 and remains the division's top contender, appeared to go easy on the tech billionaire throughout the session. Even so, Zuckerberg got a moment to show off his striking and wrestling, at one point throwing Dvalishvili into the lake. This marks the second time the pair have sparred publicly, having first done rounds together in December 2025.Zuckerberg has built a reputation over the past few years for training regularly in MMA and jiujitsu, often sparring with some of the sport's most accomplished fighters. His dedication to the sport previously prompted UFC president Dana White to remark that the Meta boss could hold his own physically against just about anyone.The viral fight comes as Zuckerberg faces scrutiny over his $300 million yacht Launchpad, which was accused of ignoring a distress call from a stranded vessel in Alaskan waters earlier this month. Mark Zuckerberg’s $390 million, 387-foot yacht Launchpad was recently booed over a reported failure to respond to a stranded boat. A Meta spokesperson has now clarified that the vessel's crew was on a different radio channel and that help was already on the way. The incident happened last Monday, August 3 evening in Alaska after a 21-foot skiff ran out of fuel between Juneau and Petersburg. While social media users criticised Mark Zuckerberg's superyacht, the company said neither Zuckerberg nor his family were on board at the time.

The pair traded blows in front of drones, videographers, and friends, with Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan casually paddling past on a canoe. Zuckerberg has built a reputation for training regularly in MMA and jiujitsu, often sparring with some of the sport's most accomplished fighters.

Article Title: Nick Long, Mayor of League City in Texas, joins H-1B visa debate; says: H-1B program should not be used by any ...
Article Text:
The debate began after Texas State University filed a notice of intent to sponsor an H-1B visa for a Public Relations Specialist position

Public universities are H-1B cap-exempt

Nick Long, Mayor of League City in Texas has joined the H-1b visa debate publicly. Long recently said in an X post that no public organisation should use the H-1B program, arguing taxpayer-funded jobs should go to taxpayers in response to Texas State University's filing for a Public Relations Specialist role. Nick Long’s comments came in response to a post announcing that the Texas State University (@txst) has filed a notice of intent to hire an H-1B Public Relations administrator.The debate began after Texas State University filed a notice of intent to sponsor an H-1B visa for a Public Relations Specialist position. The filing prompted Scott Bowen, Republican nominee for Texas House of Representatives, to share the post on his timeline writing: “Texas State graduates hundreds of communication majors every year. Not one of them was qualified for this job?”.Nick Long quoted the post and wrote: “No public entity should be using H-1B program. Taxpayers should get taxpayer funded jobs”.Under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA § 214(g)(5)(A) and (B)), certain categories of H1B petitions are exempt from the annual numerical cap of 65,000 (plus 20,000 master's cap). This means they can sponsor eligible foreign workers for H-1B visas throughout the year without participating in the annual lottery.The exemption also applies to nonprofit entities affiliated with higher education institutions and certain nonprofit or government research organisations.In other news, a new research indicates a projected decline in international student enrollment for Fall 2026. Preliminary analysis by NAFSA: Association of International Educators and JB International shows cascading effects on US economic contribution and jobs supported. This downturn reflects the convergence of several headwinds: declining application volumes, persistent visa appointment bottlenecks, and newly restrictive immigration policy changes.
Article Summary: The debate began after Texas State University filed a notice of intent to sponsor an H-1B visa for a Public Relations Specialist position. Nick Long quoted the post and wrote: “No public entity should be using H- 1B program. Taxpayers should get taxpayer funded jobs’

Article Title: Few years ago, US store owner found 97 ultra rare vintage Mario game cartridges: They are now up for auction
Article Text:
A casual scrap-metal purchase turns into a ‘Holy Grail’

Cassettes get record-breaking grades from authenticators

Auction details and charity announcement

A box of 97 factory-fresh vintage Nintendo video games that sat untouched in a US storage for years has officially hit the auction block, putting one of the most unusual discoveries in retro gaming history up for public bidding on Friday (August 14). According to a report, this collection consists of 97 uncirculated copies of the classic Super Mario Bros. / Duck Hunt combination cartridge. Originally released for the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) in 1988, these specific copies carry a 1993 manufacturing date – two years after the title was thought to be discontinued, essentially making them the last known production run and a previously undocumented variant in gaming archives. The online sale began through Goldin's Pop Culture Auction and will run through September 9.The discovery was made when Kevin Braun, owner of One Stop Wonders in Waukesha, Wisconsin, asked long-time Nintendo collector and Nintendo Wire founder Jason Ganos to help appraise and sell common games and Pokémon cards. During the conversation, Braun brought up a forgotten box of cartridges he had previously bought from a customer whose family originally saved them for scrap metal.When Ganos examined the games, he discovered that all 97 copies were in flawless, unplayed condition. As Nintendo officially ended standard production of the combination bundle in 1991, collectors believe this unexpected 1993 batch was produced either as warranty replacement inventory or for a retail store promotion that never made it to shelves.Realising the potential value of the uncirculated batch, Ganos personally transported all 97 game cartridges in his carry-on luggage to California for professional authentication and grading. Examiners at Professional Sports Authenticator (PSA) graded the entire batch, awarding five of the 97 cartridges a flawless “Gem Mint 10.” According to Ganos, PSA had never previously awarded a perfect 10 grade to an original NES cartridge.While high-grade vintage video games have commanded six-figure sums in recent years, Ganos noted that it is difficult to predict the final hammer price because uncirculated, high-graded NES cartridges with this specific production history have never appeared on the public market before.Braun and Ganos are offering the majority of the cartridges in the current sale, including three of the five copies awarded the historic perfect 10 grade. Both men are retaining one perfect-grade copy each alongside select high 9-rated copies for their personal collections.
Article Summary: A box of 97 factory-fresh vintage Nintendo video games has officially hit the auction block. The collection consists of 97 uncirculated copies of the classic Super Mario Bros. / Duck Hunt combination cartridge. These specific copies carry a 1993 manufacturing date – two years after the title was thought to be discontinued. The online sale began through Goldin's Pop Culture Auction and will run through September 9.

Article Title: US Immigration authority to H1-B visa holders, students and other visa holders: These forms will be rejected starting September 15
Article Text:

What are Form I-539 and Form I-765

USCIS says no grace period for form change

“If filing Form I-539, please note that USCIS will:

Accept the 08/28/24 edition of Form I-539 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted before Sept. 15, 2026;

Reject the 08/28/24 edition of Form I-539 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted on or after Sept. 15, 2026; and

Only accept the 09/15/26 edition of Form I-539 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted on or after Sept. 15, 2026.

Accept the 08/21/25 edition of Form I-765 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted before Sept. 15, 2026;

Reject the 08/21/25 edition of Form I-765 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted on or after Sept. 15, 2026; and

Only accept the 09/15/26 edition of Form I-765 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted on or after Sept. 15, 2026."

The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has announced that two of its important immigration forms will be replaced with new editions, starting September 15. The change will be applicable to Form I-539, Application to Extend/Change Nonimmigrant Status, and Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization (edition date for both: 09/15/26). The agency further stated that from September 15, it will only accept the 09/15/26 editions of these forms, clarifying that applications with old forms will get rejected. In its official announcement, the immigration authority said that the revised forms “align with the recently published Establishing a Fixed Time Period of Admission and an Extension of Stay Procedure for Nonimmigrant Academic Students, Exchange Visitors, and Representatives of Foreign Information Media final rule”.“On Sept. 15, 2026, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services will publish revised editions of Form I-539, Application to Extend/Change Nonimmigrant Status, and Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization (edition date for both: 09/15/26),” the agency said adding “The 09/15/26 editions of Form I-539 and Form I-765 replace the 08/28/24 edition of Form I-539 and the 08/21/25 edition of Form I-765”.Used by H-1B visa holders, students and other visa holders, the I-539 form is for immigration status, while the I-765 form is for work authorization.Form I-539: Used to extend or change a nonimmigrant visa status while in the US. An H-1B worker generally does not use I-765 for their H-1B work authorization. However, certain H-4 spouses may use I-765 to apply for an Employment Authorization Document (EAD), if they meet the eligibility requirements.In the announcement, USCIS further clarifies that there is no grace period for the revised editions of Form I-539 and Form I-765 because the revised editions are necessary for USCIS to apply the final rule.“Because there will be no grace period, USCIS is providing preview versions of the 09/15/26 editions of Form I-539 and Form I-765 with their instructions. Article Title: Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration suspends 14 licences linked to Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart after food safety checks
Article Text:
Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration suspends 14 licences linked to Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart after food safety checks

Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart licences suspended

Zepto outlet in Pune found with expired food

Blinkit facilities flagged over temperature, hygiene

Zepto and Instamart outlets face food storage violations

The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the licences of 14 food businesses linked to quick-commerce platforms Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart. The development comes after a statewide inspection drive on August 13 that found several food safety and hygiene violations. According to a report by PTI, the inspection drive covered 86 establishments involved in storing, selling and delivering food through online platforms. The inspections covered food storage, temperature control, cleanliness, pest control, worker hygiene, food safety records and compliance with required food handling practices.As reported by PTI, the FDA also issued 60 improvement notices and directed one facility to temporarily stop operations, the news agency stated.Of the 14 suspended licences, five were linked to Blinkit, five to Zepto and two to Instamart. One licence each was suspended for Bhagwati Stores and Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd. The FDA said its inspections focused on whether food businesses were following prescribed safety and hygiene rules while storing and handling products.Officials checked storage conditions, temperature control, cleanliness, pest management and personal hygiene of food workers.They also checked food safety records, display of licences and inventory systems such as First In, First Out (FIFO) and First Expired, First Out (FEFO).In Pune, the FDA suspended the licence of a Zepto outlet in Lohegaon after inspectors found food products stored beyond their declared "use by" dates. Officials also found unhygienic storage conditions, inadequate pest control and lapses in the personal hygiene of workers. The FDA said the response given by the company during the hearing was unsatisfactory.Another Pune facility operated by Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd was found to have a cockroach infestation. Inspectors also reported problems with cold-chain maintenance for frozen products and deficiencies in hygiene and pest control.A Blinkit facility in Malad, Mumbai, was found operating with chiller temperatures above the prescribed limit. The FDA also found that around 40 food handlers had not undergone mandatory medical examinations, and the required records were not available.Officials further found that some workers were not using protective equipment such as gloves, aprons and head coverings. Damaged storage racks, poor organisation and inadequate separation of different food categories were also reported.At another Blinkit facility in Ghatkopar, inspectors found issues involving drainage, waste disposal, temperature control and housekeeping. The outlet scored 46% during the inspection and was classified as non-compliant.Inspections at Zepto facilities in Mulund and Goregaon found deficiencies related to food storage, temperature management, cleanliness and licence display. At an Instamart outlet in Andheri, inspectors found food packets stored directly on the floor. The FDA also reported inadequate storage space, overcrowding and problems with hygiene and temperature control.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration has suspended licences of 14 food businesses linked to Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart. The development comes after a statewide inspection drive on August 13 that found several food safety and hygiene violations. The inspections covered food storage, temperature control, cleanliness, pest control, worker hygiene and compliance with required food handling practices.

Article Title: Apple threat notifications: What is mercenary spyware and how to protect against it
Article Text:
What exactly is Apple's threat notification

What to do if you get Apple threat notification

General security tips for everyone

Apple recently sent notifications to customers who it suspected to have been targeted with spyware in their devices. The tech giant later confirmed to multiple publications that it sent out the notifications on Thursday to users targeted in 110 countries. By sending these alerts, the company reminded users about one of the most sophisticated digital threats currently in existence: mercenary spyware. If you are one of those who got the term “Apple threat notification” flashing on your screen and wondered what it actually means, here's a breakdown of what these alerts are, why they are sent and what you should do if you ever receive one.Apple threat notifications exist for one specific purpose: to warn and assist users who may have been individually targeted by spyware attacks. In this case, it was a notification for mercenary spyware. These operations are far more advanced than regular cybercrime, and attackers behind them pour in exceptional resources to go after a very small, specific group of people and their devices.Apple says that these attacks cost millions of dollars to carry out and often don’t stay active for very long, which actually makes them harder to detect and stop in time.The good news, though, is that the majority of users will never come across this kind of attack in their lifetime.Citing public reporting and research conducted by civil society groups, cybersecurity researchers, and journalists over the years, Apple says that this level of individually targeted, high-cost cyberattacks has typically been linked to state actors, including private firms that build mercenary spyware for governments, such as the NSO Group's well-known Pegasus tool. While only a small number of individuals end up being targeted, usually journalists, activists, politicians, and diplomats, these attacks are happening constantly and across the globe.If you ever receive one of these alerts, Apple provides extra guidance and recommends steps you can take to secure your accounts and devices, including turning on Lockdown Mode. The company also strongly recommends reaching out to expert organisations for help, such as the Digital Security Helpline run by the nonprofit Access Now, which offers round-the-clock emergency security assistance.While most people will never encounter mercenary spyware, it's still worth following some basic cybersecurity habits.The first is to keep your devices updated with the latest software so you're covered by the newest security patches, and protect them with a passcode, Face ID, or Touch ID.The second most important thing to do is to turn on two-factor authentication along with a strong password for your Apple Account, and enable Stolen Device Protection for extra peace of mind.While Apple doesn’t allow installing apps from third-party stores, ensure that you download apps only from the App Store, use strong and unique passwords across your accounts, opt for passkeys wherever they're availableFinally, Avoid clicking on links or opening attachments sent by unknown senders.
Article Summary: Apple recently sent notifications to customers who it suspected to have been targeted with spyware in their devices. The tech giant confirmed to multiple publications that it sent out the notifications on Thursday to users targeted in 110 countries. By sending these alerts, the company reminded users about one of the most sophisticated digital threats currently in existence: mercenary spyware.

Article Title: In 2024, a Google Maps User was planning a trip using the app; and what he found was a giant meteorite crater that…
Article Text:
Representative Image

Shatter cones and melt rock: how geologists confirmed the Quebec impact crater

Why Uhackatik is one of the biggest meteorite crater discoveries in years

Joël Lapointe was doing something entirely ordinary. The Canadian amateur astronomer had Google Maps open in 2024, scrolling through Quebec's Côte-Nord region to plan hiking routes for a camping trip. Somewhere north of Magpie, around Lake Marsal, the terrain stopped looking like terrain. It looked like a ring—a near-perfect circular scar pressed into the forest, roughly 25km across. His first instinct was to talk himself out of it. Surely someone had already logged this. Lapointe went through the crater databases he knew of and came up empty, so he filed a report with Impact Earth, a crowdsourced crater registry run out of Western University in Ontario. Two years later, that hunch has a name. The structure is now called Uhackatik, and geologists say a meteorite carved it out about 390 million years ago.Planetary geologist Gordon Osinski, who manages Impact Earth, was sceptical at first—most reports he receives turn out to be nothing. He co-led an expedition to the site anyway in October 2025, and the terrain fought back. Osinski, who has done 25 Arctic expeditions across six continents, described it as among the toughest he has attempted, with brutal ground and relentless bugs.Day two settled it. The team found shatter cones, the branching fracture patterns that form when a shockwave rips through rock and point back towards the impact. They also found large exposures of impact melt rock—stone liquefied by the strike, then recooled—which usually erodes away long before anyone gets to see it. Traces of zircon added to the case.Only about 200 impact craters have been confirmed worldwide, and one or two turn up annually, typically in the 5–10km range. Uhackatik is several times that. Osinski reckons the last find of comparable scale was the Hiawatha structure spotted under Greenland's ice in 2018, whose size and origin remain disputed. This one isn't ambiguous.The 390-million-year date puts the impact well before dinosaurs existed—the earliest species appear around 230 million years ago. The name came after consultation with the Innu Council of Ekuanitshit, on whose traditional lands it sits. Findings go to the Meteoritical Society's annual meeting in Frankfurt this month, ahead of peer review.Google Maps and Google Earth have cracked open discoveries beforeSatellite imagery has form here. Egypt's remarkably intact Kamil Crater surfaced through a Google Earth search in 2008. That same year, palaeoanthropologist Lee Berger used it to pinpoint the South African cave system that yielded Australopithecus sediba.As Lapointe put it, ordinary citizens don't find 390-million-year-old craters every day.
Article Summary: A Canadian amateur astronomer found a crater on Google Maps in 2024. The structure is now called Uhackatik, and geologists say a meteorite carved it out about 390 million years ago. The 390-million-year date puts the impact well before dinosaurs existed.

Article Title: Fireflies.ai brings its AI notetaker to the inbox with Email Assistant, now free on all plans
Article Text:
Meeting context is the part rival AI email tools can't copy

Fireflies.ai, the AI meeting assistant used by more than 20 million people and teams at 75% of Fortune 500 companies, has moved into the inbox. On Friday the company launched Email Assistant, which plugs into Gmail or Outlook and treats email the way it already treats calls—sorting what lands, labelling it by priority, and dropping drafted replies into the thread before you get to them.The pitch rests on a familiar arithmetic. Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index found the average worker receives 117 emails a day, with 40% of people online at 6am already checking mail and nearly a third back at it by 10pm—the "infinite workday" Microsoft has been warning about. Fireflies' argument is simpler than most: if it sat in on the call, it already knows what the reply should say.That is the actual differentiator here. When a prospect or candidate follows up on something discussed weeks ago, Email Assistant pulls from both the thread and past meetings with that person, so users aren't reconstructing the conversation from memory. Auto Labels triages incoming mail without touching existing rules or filters. Auto Draft Replies writes in a tone set through custom Writing Instructions, and nothing sends without review. If a sent email goes quiet, a follow-up is drafted in the same thread after a waiting period you configure. AskFred handles plain-English requests—find an email, summarise a thread, pull this week's action items.Insights from email now also feed the Daily Brief alongside meetings and Slack. Meeting Prep, Tasks and AI Skills will draw on email context in the coming months.Email Assistant is available today across all plans, including the free tier. Pro starts at Rs 955 per seat per month, billed annually. Fireflies says it does not train its models on customer data.
Article Summary: Fireflies.ai's Email Assistant plugs into Gmail or Outlook and treats email the way it already treats calls. It pulls from both the thread and past meetings with that person, so users aren't reconstructing the conversation from memory. Email Assistant is available today across all plans, including the free tier.

Article Title: Trump’s family crypto venture, World Liberty Financial gets conditional US bank charter approval
Article Text:
USD1 stablecoin could move under World Liberty

OCC sets conditions for the bank

A US banking regulator has conditionally approved a bank charter application linked to President Donald Trump and his family's crypto venture, World Liberty Financial. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) said it granted preliminary approval to World Liberty Trust Company's application for a national trust charter. The company applied for the charter in January this year. If it receives final approval, the trust bank would be able to hold and manage assets for customers and settle payments. The charter would also allow World Liberty to directly issue its USD1 stablecoin and hold the US dollar assets backing it.According to a report by Reuters, the OCC published a letter on August 14 granting conditional preliminary approval to World Liberty Trust Company's application for a national trust charter. However, the approval is not yet final. The company must meet conditions set by the regulator before receiving the charter.The charter could give World Liberty more control over its USD1 stablecoin business. If approved, World Liberty Trust could directly issue USD1 and hold the US dollar assets that support the stablecoin. Those activities are currently handled by business partner BitGo.Welcoming the decision, Zach Witkoff, president and chairman of World Liberty Trust, said: "A national trust bank brings USD1 issuance, custody, and reserve management together under OCC supervision, examined on the same standards that have governed banks for generations.We welcome continuous scrutiny from Federal regulators for many years to come".As mentioned above, the preliminary approval comes with several conditions. World Liberty Trust must notify the OCC about major changes to its business plan, maintain at least $20 million in capital and hire a qualified employee to serve as its internal audit manager.The OCC also addressed concerns about non-US investors in World Liberty Financial.The regulator said those investors were not considered principal shareholders of the proposed bank. It also said several investors had signed "passivity agreements" promising not to control or influence the bank's operations or decisions. One of those signatories was Eric Trump, the president's son, who signed as president of a Trump-family affiliated investment vehicle.
Article Summary: OCC conditionally approves World Liberty Trust Company's application for a national trust charter. If approved, the trust bank would be able to hold and manage assets for customers and settle payments. The charter would also allow World Liberty to directly issue its USD1 stablecoin and hold the US dollar assets backing it.

Article Title: OpenAI's 612-megawatt facility, ranked among the world's biggest AI data centres, abandons plan to cool servers with recycled water as ...
Article Text:
OpenAI's first ChatGPT-powered device is said to be a smart speaker

What made OpenAI walkaway from recycled water plan

OpenAI has abandoned plans to cool its planned S7 data center in Sydney, Australia, with recycled water. OpenAI nixed the plans in favor of a closed-loop liquid cooling system. According to a report in Reuters, Developers of a massive data centre OpenAI wants to build in Australia have abandoned plans to cool it with recycled water, switching to a more ​energy-intensive method that undercuts government efforts to curb the booming sector's drain on resources.The 612-megawatt 'S7' facility, planned as one of the largest data hubs in the world, initially aimed to tap Sydney’s treated wastewater to chill its servers, which would have reduced dependence on potable water sources and significantly lowered the cooling system's energy requirements. The move was designed to avoid depleting local drinking supplies while minimizing electricity use, according to planning documents filed in April.However, after failing to secure planning permission to build a pipeline to serve the data center, NextDC, the developer, decided to change its plans. Australian data centre operator NEXTDC told Reuters that it walked away from negotiations with local utilities after hitting regulatory roadblocks over the permits needed to construct a dedicated wastewater pipeline. In December 2025, OpenAI and NextDC announced that they had signed a Memorandum of Understanding that would see the ChatGPT-maker use some of the data center’s capacity, with the option to scale over time."Recycled water ... has real merit and it can support lower PUE and better overall sustainability and NEXTDC considers it wherever that infrastructure exists," CEO Craig Scroggie said in an email. PUE, or ​power usage effectiveness, is a closely watched metric of energy used for cooling and other overheads beyond computing. "Potential sources were canvassed in early planning. In Western Sydney, the enabling infrastructure . .. is not yet in ​place," Scroggie is said to have added.The S7 datacentre facility will now rely on a closed-loop liquid cooling system that circulates coolant directly across processing chips and dissipates heat into the air using fans. While the revised system uses no drinking water, analysts say the fan arrays will consume significantly more electricity at a time when Sydney's grid operator warns transmission capacity is already stretched thin by data centre demand.As per launch release S7 datacenter is expected to deliver thousands of direct and indirect jobs over the course of its construction, as well as ongoing technical, manufacturing, engineering and operational roles.
Article Summary: OpenAI abandons plans to cool data center in Australia with recycled water. Instead, it will rely on a closed-loop liquid cooling system that circulates coolant directly across processing chips and dissipates heat into the air using fans. The move was designed to avoid depleting local drinking supplies while minimizing electricity use, according to planning documents.

Article Title: Global innovation hub to AI skills training for 1 cr youth: PM Modi outlines nation's tech ambitions
Article Text:
Target of 100 GW of nuclear energy by 2047, 5 new nuclear reactors to be operational within 6-7 years: PM Modi

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday put technology and innovation at the heart of India's growth ambitions, calling for leadership in emerging technologies and announcing AI skilling for one crore youth over the next one year.Addressing the nation on the 80th Independence Day, Modi said new frontiers in artificial intelligence, quantum computing, space, robotics and data centres are opening up rapidly, and stressed the need for the country to take the lead in technology and innovation.Outlining a seven-point framework for 'Viksit Bharat' - India's goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047 - the PM identified technology and innovation as the third 'shakti' of the "Sapta Dhara" vision, saying rapid advances in artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, space, robotics and data centres are creating new opportunities."Today, the world is one of AI, quantum, space, robotics and data centres. New areas have opened up," the prime minister said.Modi further said India must respond to the challenges posed by emerging technologies by becoming a global innovation hub rather than merely a market for the world."We must become a global hub for innovation", he emphasised.Modi said India had already demonstrated, to the world, its capabilities in UPI and digital public infrastructure, and now needs to emerge as a force in 'digital public technologies'."India must lead in next-generation communications technology. Made-in-India 6G should reach every corner, and that should be our goal," he said.Placing a strong emphasis on preparing India's youth for the artificial intelligence-driven economy, Modi announced a large-scale skilling push."In the coming one year, we will work to provide AI skills training to one crore youth, so that India's youth can lead in the AI era," Modi said.The PM noted that energy security was becoming increasingly critical to India's technological ambitions, with chips, AI and data centres requiring vast amounts of electricity.He identified nuclear energy as a key component of energy security, and said the country is targeting 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047, and plans to commission five new reactors this decade.Modi said cybersecurity was becoming a concern for every household.It is a domain of defence that offers an opportunity to harness the capabilities of India's youth, both for the country and the world, he pointed out.The prime minister also pointed to the changing nature of warfare, saying modern conflicts could target critical infrastructure such as refineries, banks and data centres rather than remain confined to borders.He said work on 'Mission Sudarshan Chakra' is progressing rapidly, and further added India's defence exports had risen nearly 50-fold.India's technology companies should aspire to become global leaders, the PM said while also calling for creation of homegrown brands that gain worldwide recognition and become synonymous with the country's identity.Modi said the government is seeking to draw young Indians towards technology from an early age, pointing to more than 10,000 'Atal Tinkering Labs' and the expansion of the startup ecosystem, itself.He also highlighted the achievements by young Indians in launching satellites and rockets."You may have seen how young Indians, averaging just 28 years of age, achieved a global first: they successfully launched their own satellite and rocket on their very first attempt, accomplishing a truly monumental feat," he said.Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-1 recently became India's first privately-developed rocket to successfully reach orbit, marking a historic milestone for the country's private space sector and commercial launch capabilities.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi calls for leadership in emerging technologies. Calls for AI skilling for one crore youth over the next one year. Target of 100 GW of nuclear energy by 2047, 5 new nuclear reactors to be operational within 6-7 years.

Plan Validity Data Benefit Status Replacement / Change Rs 299 28 days 1.5GB/day Discontinued Shifted to Rs 349 pack (same benefits, ~16% higher price) Rs 319 30 days 1.5GB/day Discontinued No direct replacement listed Rs 579 56 days 1.5GB/day Discontinued Withdrawn Rs 619 69 days 1.5GB/day Discontinued Withdrawn Rs 649 56 days 2GB/day Discontinued Withdrawn Rs 799 77 days 1.5GB/day / 2GB/day Discontinued Withdrawn Rs 859 Long-term 2GB/day Repriced Now Rs 899 Rs 199 / Rs 219 Entry-level Lower data packs Unchanged Still available

Airtel has undertaken one of its biggest prepaid portfolio rationalisations in recent years discontinuing several recharge plans including the popular Rs 299 pack. The move effectively raises Airtel’s tariffs by 3%-4% and will support average revenue per user (ARPU) growth in the coming quarters, analysts said. Bharti Airtel reported a 37.3% increase in profit after tax to Rs 8,167 crore in the June quarter, driven by strong growth across its India and Africa operations. Revenue from operations rose 18.3% to Rs 58,539 crore from Rs 49,462.6 crore in the year-ago quarter.The telco withdrew four prepaid plans priced at Rs 299, Rs 579, Rs 619 and Rs 649. The company’s subscribers for the popular Rs 299 plan will now have to opt for the Rs 349 pack, implying a price increase of around 16%. The company has also pulled four of its 1.5GB/day plans, including Rs 319 plan (30-day), Rs 579 (56-day), Rs 619 (69-day) and Rs 799 (77-day) plan; and discontinued 2GB/day plan of Rs 649 (56-day), Rs 619 (69-day) and Rs 799 (77-day) plan; and discontinued 2GB/day plan of Rs 649 (56-day), according to the latest listing on the telco’s website. The Rs 859 plan has been repriced to Rs 899, according to channel checks done by ET.The most significant impact will be felt by users of the Rs 299 plan, which long served as Airtel’s entry-level unlimited 28-day pack, offering 1.5 GB of data per day. With this plan now retired, subscribers must shift to the Rs 349 pack—which offers identical benefits—marking a steep 16% price increase. As a result, the Rs 349 recharge now is Airtel’s cheapest unlimited 28-day daily data prepaid option.Meanwhile, Airtel has also adjusted long-term tariffs, repricing the Rs 859 plan to Rs 899. However, ultra-low-end entry plans, such as the Rs 199 and Rs 219 packs, remain untouched for now.The company has also withdrawn certain 56-day and 90-day prepaid plans that saw relatively low customer adoption, indicating a broader effort to simplify its prepaid portfolio.This rationalisation comes weeks after Airtel introduced its high-speed postpaid Fastlane plan with a focus to drive customer premiumisation and ARPU growth.Shashwat Sharma, MD & CEO, Airtel India, said that the industry's pricing architecture needs a repair with a data consumption-driven charging mechanism. “I think the pricing architecture will have to repair with charging for data consumption becoming the norm if we are to see this kind of long-term sustainability,” Sharma had said during the company’s recent earnings call. “This is paramount for sustained ARPU growth in the longer term. ”JM Financial told ET that other telecom companies have not made any changes so far, but are likely to follow Bharti Airtel which removed select entry-level prepaid data plans across 28–60 day validity. The domestic brokerage believes this is not an across-the-board tariff hike. Instead, it is plan modification to push subscribers to upgrade to higher GB and higher ARPU plans (by making Rs 349 28-day 1.5GB/day as its entry-level data plan).The brokerage reportedly pointed to a similar move in August last year, when Airtel had withdrawn its Rs 249 entry level 1GB/day 28-day plan from digital channels. It also had discontinued its Rs 249 24-day plan 1GB/day, making Rs 299 28-day 1GB/day as its entry-level data plan, which has now been discontinued.
Article Summary: Airtel has withdrawn four prepaid plans priced at Rs 299, Rs 579, Rs 619 and Rs 649. The company’s subscribers for the popular Rs 299 plan will now have to opt for the Rs 349 pack, implying a price increase of around 16%. The company has also pulled four of its 1.5GB/day plans.
